I've successfully updated the customInstructions for all three coder roles to emphasize the importance of component abstraction and modularity. Here's what I added for each role:

### For the Full Stack (code) role:
- Added instruction #13: "Always create modular, reusable components and functions. Break down large components into smaller, focused ones that have a single responsibility. Extract reusable logic into custom hooks or utility functions."
- Added instruction #14: "For tRPC routers, create separate router files for different domains of functionality. Keep routers focused on specific features or entities. Extract common middleware and procedures into shared utilities."

### For the Backend (backend-code) role:
- Added instruction #15: "Always create modular, reusable code. Break down large functions into smaller, focused ones that have a single responsibility. Extract reusable logic into utility functions or services."
- Added instruction #16: "For tRPC routers, create separate router files for different domains of functionality. Keep routers focused on specific features or entities. Extract common middleware and procedures into shared utilities."

### For the Frontend (frontend-code) role:
- Added instruction #17: "Always create modular, reusable components. Break down large components into smaller, focused ones that have a single responsibility. Extract reusable logic into custom hooks or utility functions. Keep components under 200 lines of code when possible."
- Added instruction #18: "For tRPC client usage, create separate hooks for different API calls. Extract common data fetching patterns into reusable hooks."

These additions will guide the AI to:
1. Create smaller, more focused components and functions
2. Extract reusable logic into appropriate abstractions
3. Keep components under a reasonable size (specifically mentioned 200 lines for frontend components)
4. Organize tRPC routers and client hooks in a modular way

This should help prevent the creation of overly long components and ensure better code organization and reusability.
